setter.name: Kim Forbes-Sobers
setter.evidence: Rep opened with 'I spoke to Kim. You had a conversation with him a few days ago, so he just gave me some brief information about you.' The prospect independently confirms it three times, including 'I put Kim through a lot just to get to this point' and 'I did let Kim know, I'm like, look, if I get assigned a different trainer, that's not really what I'm looking for.'

prospect.name: Daniel
prospect.location: Near Fort Leavenworth, Kansas, USA (Central time)
prospect.occupation: United States Army, 22 years' service, currently in an HR and personnel/pay administration role; approaching retirement eligibility
prospect.family_status: Lives alone in a 170-year-old house. Son aged 18, just graduated high school, lives with his mother in Atlanta, Type 1 diabetic, roughly 205 lb and the same height as his father. Has a sister.
prospect.training_background: Competitive figure skater before enlisting, two national titles at 26, on the ice six days a week. Joined the Army at 30 weighing 160 lb; peaked at 230 lb and is now 211 lb. Has free access to the base gym about a mile away but trains without structure — 'there's, you know, 85 machines and 100 weights... I always feel like I don't really have a focus.' Currently passes Army physical fitness requirements with no limitations. Hired vShred roughly a year ago and injured himself three times during their exercises, each time requiring physical therapy. Has tried a couple of Trevor's kettlebell movements from the videos.
prospect.medical: Self-reported body fat 31-32% (Hume band and scale), described as over 60 lb of fat. Currently on prescribed anti-cholesterol medication. Low testosterone; has previously done testosterone replacement therapy and dislikes it; clinicians are again discussing hormone therapy. Has taken antidepressants in the past, not currently. Chronic sleep-onset insomnia going back to his twenties, investigated with a sleep study. Historic Achilles tendinitis and currently attending physical therapy to strengthen weak areas and prevent a flare-up. Reports knee tenderness after high-volume squatting and limited squat depth. States he has no functional limitations.

signals: Explicitly wants a former self back — a two-time national-title figure skater now 50 lb heavier: 'at one point I was in really good shape'.
Carries visible regret about a slow twenty-year decline: 'it's that slow creep that is letting me realize that things are going negative'.
Gym envy and a self-described cycle of discouragement: 'I'm so tired of being in the gym and envying what other people look like'.
Not the_preserver despite age and medical management: the goal is reversal and fat loss, not holding on to function.
Not the_medically_constrained: the conditions are chronic and managed rather than blocking, and no clinician has ruled anything out.

goals.text: Drop body fat from 31-32% — 'when they put that into pounds, it turns out to be like over 60 pounds of fat. I'm like, that is just unacceptable.'
Come off cholesterol medication and raise testosterone without hormone therapy — 'there's got to be a more natural way to boost testosterone than just being on hormone therapy'
Show his 18-year-old son that a body like his can be changed, so the son believes he can do it too — 'I need to do it for both of us'
Not be worse off at 60 and 75 — 'my body indicators... are telling me that I'm in a negative trajectory'
Become someone who trains regardless of circumstances — 'I want to get to the point where it's a guarantee that I'm going to work out regardless of what's going on'
Meet Army body-fat and fitness standards and reach retirement without being separated for fitness
Be comfortable with his shirt off by Christmas
Fix sleep — get to bed at 10 and up at 6
Stop the cycle of injury and self-doubt

pains.text: Trains without structure or focus and therefore sees no results, then quits — 'because of the lack of focus, I don't see the results I'm hoping for, and then I get discouraged and stopped'

Injured three times on the previous online programme because the exercises were not explained — 'there were three times I had to go to physical therapy because I injured something during the exercises because I didn't understand them'
Chronic sleep-onset insomnia since his twenties, with daytime fatigue — 'I'd be like, okay, it's two in the morning, I've been here since 10 o'clock at night, can I please fall asleep?'
On cholesterol medication and being steered toward hormone therapy, both of which he resents
Slow twenty-year weight gain from 160 lb to a 230 lb peak, currently 211 lb at 31-32% body fat
Overwhelmed by the gym environment — 'I'll walk into a gym and it's overwhelming... there's 85 machines and 100 weights'
Knows what to do but not how to implement it — 'you're telling me stuff I know, I just don't know how to implement them'
Job pressure in an HR/pay role he was not trained for and is understaffed in
Fear that his son, 18 and already at his father's weight, follows the same trajectory
New Defense Secretary separating soldiers who fail body-fat and fitness standards, months from his retirement
Doubted he was even eligible — the advertising asks for men 30-45 and he is 52

objections.raw_quote: one of his videos said he was looking for men between the ages of like 30 and 45. And I messaged him, I'm like, well, I'm 52. So I don't want to waste your time if I'm not, you know, in your group, or your target audience.
objections.rep_response: Countered with a peer example rather than addressing the advertised range — 'Two days ago, I had a call with a 69-year-old. He's not slowing down, man.' Later reinforced with 'we have different guys. We have former athletes, but everybody that's coming in, they lack something.'

objections.raw_quote: So for the Army, though, starting next week, I'm in Estonia for three weeks. So I'm in Estonia from July 11th to August 1st... I don't know if it makes more sense to start in August. I don't necessarily delay it, but I think it might make more sense in August because I don't know what my connectivity is going to be like in Estonia.
objections.rep_response: Asked 'Why would you say it would make more sense to start in August?', established the concern was Zoom connectivity rather than equipment, then explained that weekly check-ins run through the app rather than live calls and that Trevor adjusts the week for travel.

objections.raw_quote: I did let Kim know, I'm like, look, if I get assigned a different trainer, that's not really what I'm looking for. I want to be assigned to Trevor
objections.rep_response: Confirmed it is Trevor one-to-one and volunteered that he personally exchanges WhatsApp numbers with clients he onboards to stay in touch.

objections.raw_quote: So, what are the payment options for them? Are there options, or what do we do for them? A credit card, usually. I don't think any of mine have 6,000 ballots on it. I'll have to look.
objections.rep_response: Said most clients pay upfront on a credit card and framed it as 'a third layer of commitment', then offered a debit card as an alternative — 'If you have it in your savings or checking account, that's totally fine.' No financial picture was taken beyond that.

offer.guarantee_mentioned: Asserted without terms: 'as I mentioned, full transformation, six months, guarantee on that, and investment for that, it's 6K.' No earlier statement of what the guarantee actually promises appears anywhere in the transcript.

prospect_financials.note: 'I don't have a problem with 6,000. It's just figuring out how to get it so I can do it all at once.' Doubts any single card has a $6,000 limit available. Says he needs to move funds and that a couple of days should be enough. No open wallet was run.

evidence: Clear verbal agreement at full price: 'I don't have a problem with 6,000' and 'So, $6,000. I got that part. So, yeah, let's get that covered.'

No payment taken and, decisively, no payment link sent — the prospect asked for one directly: 'So, are you going to send me a link for payment and stuff?' and the rep did not send it, answering 'I need to get you onboarded and so on. So, do you have that right now with you?'
The verbal-agreement-plus-link close rule therefore does not apply; the link half never happened.
A second call was booked live for Monday at 10:00 Central and the calendar invite was confirmed received on the call: 'Oh, there it is. Yep. Monday.'
The Trevor onboarding call was explicitly deferred: 'this week it's going to be impossible because it's already Friday and tomorrow is holidays.'
Counter-evidence on certainty: the only unresolved item is liquidity, not desire — he needs to move funds and does not think a single card carries $6,000 of available credit.
outcome.next_step: Second call Monday 10:00 Central, calendar invite sent and confirmed, prospect to have moved $6,000 into an accessible account by then. Note he leaves for Estonia on 11 July.

notable.note: The most winnable call in the batch and it was not closed. The prospect agreed to $6,000 at full price, asked unprompted for a payment link, and did not get one — the rep pivoted to booking a second call three days later instead of sending the link or taking a card, and also deferred the Trevor onboarding call because of the holiday. Separately and more seriously, the rep told a prospect on prescribed statin therapy that the goal is to come off it: 'you're taking meds for cholesterol, right? Yeah. We want to quit that... it is possible to ditch that,' and then affirmed the prospect's framing that the pharmaceutical industry 'wants customers and not cures'. The prospect's response was 'I refuse. I'm not doing it anymore.' Also worth escalating: the prospect nearly disqualified himself before booking because Trevor's advertising specifies men aged 30-45 and he is 52 — a stated target range that is costing appointments from a demographic that converts.

quality.notes: Severe and sustained inversion. Long stretches of the rep's presentation are attributed to 'Daniel's iPhone' and much of the prospect's answering is attributed to the rep — the nutrition pillar, the accountability pillar and parts of the price exchange are all misattributed. Role was resolved from content throughout. The prospect appears only as the device label 'Daniel's iPhone'; his first name is recovered from the rep addressing him at 00:33:14 ('All right, Daniel'). Audio itself is clean and the recording is complete, ending on a normal sign-off.
